author: John Badman
title: Fast-moving storm floods streets, downs power lines across Riverbend - NewsBreak
text: WOOD RIVER — A brief but powerful storm moved through the Riverbend on Tuesday afternoon, flooding streets, downing power lines, and knocking out traffic signals in much of East Alton and Wood River. The Wood River 911 center lost power for a time at about 2:30 p.m., and lightning strikes to buildings were reported in both Wood River and Moro. The St. John United Church of Christ at 228 N. 6th Street in Wood River was seen being struck by lightning. Wood River firefighters spent 45 minutes checking every part of the church, even the bell tower, but found no major damage. Lightning was also reported to have struck a house on Heritage Road in Moro, but the damage was limited at that residence. In the intersection of Condit Street and Park Avenue in Wood River, residents were taking matters into their own hands, using rakes and shovels to try and clear leaves from sewer drains that were causing flooding in the intersection. On Old St. Louis Road in Wood River, a power pole was blown sideways, causing it to land on another power pole. Ameren was on the scene there, planning to make repairs. A tree reportedly landed on power lines on Niagara Street in East Alton. In Alton, heavy rain caused flash flooding in streets, and cars were splashing through the high water on Main Street and East Broadway. Alton firefighters responded to a tree limb that had fallen on power lines and was on fire at Ohio Street and E. Doerr Avenue. Firefighters jumped as the fire in the lines suddenly sparked with a loud boom, extinguishing its own fire. No injuries were reported.
